Additionally, during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, we also recorded an impairment charge of $29 million on certain long-lived assets related to the exit of a business, a $15 million charge to earnings related to legal matters and $8 million of losses associated with the increase in the fair value of the contingent consideration accrual associated with previous acquisitions.

prov.text: SG&A consists principally of the costs associated with our sales and marketing efforts, billing operations, credit loss expense and general management and administrative support as well as administrative facility costs.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net
nonop.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, interest expense, net decreased by $5 million compared to the prior year period primarily due to lower interest rates associated with our indebtedness and higher interest income due to higher cash balances.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, interest expense, net decreased by $13 million compared to the prior year period primarily due to lower interest rates associated with our indebtedness and the repayment in full of the outstanding indebtedness under our $600 million of 3.50% senior notes, which matured on March 30, 2025.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $1.5 billion and $1.4 billion, respectively. The $65 million increase in net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year period, was primarily a result of increased operating income being partially offset by the timing of net working capital and the prior year period including a $46 million gain from a payroll tax credit under the CARES Act.

Days sales outstanding, a measure of billing and collection efficiency, was 51 days as of September 30, 2026, 48 days as of December 31, 2025 and 47 days as of September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to a shift in payer mix associated with outstanding receivables from client payers.

sbc.text: • $6 million of excess tax benefits associated with stock-based compensation arrangements, recorded in income tax expense, or $0.05 per diluted share.

wc.text: We believe that our cash and cash equivalents and cash from operations, together with our borrowing capacity under our credit facilities, will provide sufficient financial flexibility to fund seasonal and other working capital requirements, capital expenditures, debt service requirements and other obligations, cash dividends on common shares, share repurchases and additional growth opportunities, including acquisitions, for the foreseeable future. However, should it become necessary, we believe that our credit profile should provide us with access to additional financing in order to fund normal business operations, make interest payments, fund additional growth opportunities, including acquisitions, and satisfy upcoming debt maturities.

capex.text: We estimate that we will invest approximately $550 million during 2026 for capital expenditures, to support and grow our existing operations, principally related to investments in laboratory equipment and facilities, including laboratory automations and information technology to support our diagnostic offerings.

net sales.heading: Net Revenues
net sales.text:
Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by 10.0% compared to the prior year period, on strong organic revenue growth.

DIS revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by 10.2% compared to the prior year period.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026:

• The increase in DIS revenues compared to the prior year period was principally driven by organic growth of 10.1%.

DIS business.text: We assess our revenue performance for our DIS business based upon, among other factors, volume (measured by test requisitions) and revenue per requisition. Each test requisition accompanies patient specimens, indicating the test(s) to be performed and the party to be billed for the test(s). Revenue per requisition is impacted by various factors, including, among other items, the impact of fee schedule changes (i.e., unit price), test mix, payer mix, business mix and the number of tests per requisition. Management uses number of requisitions and revenue per requisition data to assist with assessing the growth and performance of the business, including understanding trends affecting number of requisitions, pricing and test mix. Therefore, we believe that information related to changes in these metrics from period to period are useful information for investors as it allows them to assess the performance of the business.

intro.text: Quest Diagnostics works across the healthcare ecosystem to create a healthier world, one life at a time. We provide diagnostic insights from the results of our laboratory testing to empower people, physicians, and organizations to take action to improve health outcomes. Derived from one of the world's largest databases of de-identifiable clinical lab results, our diagnostic insights reveal new avenues to identify and treat disease, inspire healthy behaviors and improve healthcare management. In the right hands and with the right context, our diagnostic insights can inspire actions that transform lives and create a healthier world.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Reimbursement from our five largest health plans totaled approximately 20%, and no one health plan accounted for 10%, of our consolidated net revenues in 2025.

Health plans typically negotiate directly or indirectly with a number of diagnostic information services providers, and represent nearly one-half of our total clinical testing volume and approximately 40% of our net revenues from diagnostic information services.

In 2025 and 2024, we derived approximately 8% and 5%, respectively, of our consolidated net revenues from capitated payment arrangements and in 2025 and 2024, we derived approximately 15% and 11%, respectively, of our testing volume from capitated payment arrangements.

Revenues generated under Medicaid and managed Medicaid programs, and through the ACA related Exchange Plans, represented approximately 8% and less than 5%, respectively, of consolidated revenues for 2025.
The DIS business for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 accounted for greater than 95% of our consolidated net revenues.

Net revenues in the Company’s DIS business accounted for greater than 95 % of the Company’s consolidated net revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 and are primarily comprised of a high volume of relatively low-dollar transactions.
The DIS business accounted for greater than 95 % of net revenues in 2025, 2024 and 2023.

Our ability to make principal and interest payments will depend on our ability to generate cash in the future.
The IT systems that we rely on may be subject to unauthorized tampering, cyberattack or other security breach.

Additionally, many of the third-party service providers we rely on use AI for a variety of purposes, which increases the risk that our sensitive and proprietary data, and the data of our patients and customers, could be inadvertently or maliciously exposed.

Suppliers and manufacturers we rely upon may experience disruptions and delays stemming from raw material and labor shortages, supply challenges and significant disruptions in transport and logistics services due to facility closures, labor constraints and other challenges.
The extent to which we may be impacted by future public health emergencies and pandemics will depend on many factors beyond our knowledge or control.
Investors are cautioned not to unduly rely on such forward-looking statements when evaluating the information presented in this document.

We rely on IT systems, some of which are dependent on services provided by third parties, to provide data and other services, including diagnostic information services for patients, clinicians and healthcare organizations, clinical testing, test ordering and reporting, billing, customer service, logistics, commercial and operational data, human resources management, legal, finance and tax compliance, and other information and processes necessary to operate and manage our business.
